details.description: Swaha Akhand Jyoti Wicks are cotton batti that are used in traditional oil lamps. These jyot wicks are made from soft, pure organic cotton. They are handmade and double twisted. Cotton Wick Jyot Batti is used worldwide to light chirags/oil lamps for meditation and spiritual prayers and add elegance to the home decor. Its smoke will purify the atmosphere and bring positivity to your mind.
details.usageInstructions:
1. Cotton wicks are used for daily pujan (jyot) when dipped in ghee/oil.
2. It can also be used in temples for lighting and prayer purposes.
3. Used during Indian festive occasions like Diwali and Navratras.

details.description: Swaha Floating Wicks brings innovation to puja products. It is the best quality oil floating wicks. The wicks are glazed with a coating of wax so that they are stiff. They are an inexpensive yet elegant decorating idea for weddings, receptions, parties, holiday celebrations or a romantic evening at home. It is very simple and easy to use.
details.usageInstructions:
1. Take a glass cup or a bowl, fill it 1/3rd with water, 1/3rd oil and drop a floating wick.
2. Light it and enjoy the fluttering wick.

details.description: Swaha Maroon Kumkum is made from turmeric. It is a unique cultural and spiritual symbol. Our Kumkum will never leave stains on your forehead. Kumkum, also known as sindoor or sindur, does not contain any chemicals to make it pure and maroon-coloured. Use this pure and natural kumkum for all your pooja needs.

Swaha Red Kumkum is made from turmeric. It is a unique cultural and spiritual symbol. Our Kumkum will never leave stains on your forehead. Kumkum is also known as sindoor or sindur. It does not contain any chemicals to make it pure and rich in colour. Use this pure and natural kumkum for all your pooja needs.
details.usageInstructions:
1. Applying it on the forehead for pooja purposes.
2. Married women apply red kumkuma to the parting of their hair above their forehead every day as a symbol of marriage.

details.description: Swaha Maya Agarbatti is made of high-quality natural ingredients. In India, burning incense is about spreading positivity all around areas, burning incense sticks is also a symbol of worshipping God and a symbol of peace and freshness. The gorgeous fragrance of exotic aroma on a woody and musky note provides a soft and gentle experience. Incense sticks, also known as agarbathi (or agarbatti) and joss sticks are the main forms of incense in India, in which an incense paste is rolled or moulded around a bamboo stick. It creates a delightful atmosphere that will brings peace and joy.
details.usageInstructions:
1. Light the end of the incense stick with the use of a match or lighter.
2. Hold the flame to the stick until the stick ignites.
3. Gently extinguish the flame by blowing or fanning.
4. The incense stick should glow red and give off a delicate fragrant smoke indicating that it is slowly burning.
